parsed.explanation: Combined national and state regime imposes universal facilities exclusion by birth sex (national order; state public-facilities law with civil cause of action and trespass arrest), border screening that can refuse entry for sex-document discrepancy and pursue lifetime fraud ineligibility, and documented custody harm (immigration forced labour/abuse; corrections hormone removal). For a family with a trans minor, the state bans gender-affirming care and school restroom rules apply by birth sex. National hate-crime and employment protections exist, and courts have blocked some orders, but no working visitor-facing remedy is documented. The worst feature is tier-1 state-imposed facilities exclusion, compounded by tier-2 custody abuse and border refusal. This sits below the 0.35 anchors but well above the 0.15 criminalization regime.

entry_documents.exposure: National screening can refuse visa/entry where documents or records show sex discrepancy or reasonable doubt; potential lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans-athlete entry ban; X markers no longer issued.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; some executive orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor's home passport may not match presentation; officer discretion can strand traveler; no documented consular remedy at border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, sexual abuse; corrections policies remove hormones and cut hair; restroom-trespass arrest led to men's-ward hold.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some court injunctions; no documented custody-specific visitor protection.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border refusal or facilities arrest can move traveler into custody systems with documented harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity; state law requires multi-occupancy restrooms/changing/sleeping by biological sex, prohibits entry, creates civil cause of action; school birth-sex restroom rule.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some cities have local nondiscrimination ordinances; national employment protection only.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal exposure in public buildings; state law adds civil liability and possible trespass arrest on refusal to leave.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors; national EO frames care as mutilation, subpoenas hospital records for patients under 19; proposed public-insurance bar.
care_services.protection: Adult care not documented as banned; some orders blocked in court.
care_services.interaction: A family with a trans minor faces care denial and record exposure; adult visitor care access uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward system; official hostility; state has no hate-crime or public-accommodation nondiscrimination law.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; national employment discrimination protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Climate raises severity of police contact; state-level recourse thin; national protections do not reach facilities or street policing.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for children; school restroom law by birth sex; national EO directs prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; hospital record subpoenas.
minors_guardians.protection: Reasonable accommodation for students unwilling to use birth-sex restroom; some court blocks.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling family with trans minor faces care denial, school restroom restrictions, and potential guardian/provider investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State lacks hate-crime statute and public-accommodation nondiscrimination; national hate-crime coverage exists but state-level reporting/outcomes not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National 2009 hate-crime statute includes gender identity; three cities have local ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Visitor reporting violence may rely on national authorities; no state-level bias-crime recourse; rate of trans-specific violence not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facilities law not documented as challenged; border fraud finding has limited waiver; state no nondiscrimination recourse; custody harm oversight absent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National courts have blocked some executive orders; passport policy under challenge; legal-aid FAQ.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court wins are partial and not visitor-facing; no documented remedy that reverses facilities exclusion or border refusal in real time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Worse than our case: it criminalizes gender presentation generally, with routine arrests, months in pretrial custody, beatings, and a capital provision. Our case lacks general presentation criminalization and capital exposure, though facilities trespass and custody harm exist.

Similar: birth-sex custody placement with reported harm, administrative-building restrictions, slow remedies. Our case adds a broader public-facilities ban and border screening, but lacks general cross-dressing criminalization; roughly comparable, perhaps slightly lower.

Our case is worse: 0.35-B involves police stops, fines and interviews but no universal facilities ban or documented custody abuse. Our tier-1 facilities exclusion plus border refusal and custody harm push below.

Far worse: 0.75-C has trained border officers, brief detention, and a working tribunal. Our case has hostile border screening, universal facilities exclusion, custody abuse, and no working visitor remedy.
Far worse: 0.95-A has equality law, audits, and no detention. Our case has state-imposed facilities exclusion, border refusal, and documented custody harm.

parsed.synthesis: The national and state regimes combine into a hostile operating system: border officers may refuse entry on sex-document doubt and pursue lifetime fraud findings; admitted visitors face birth-sex facilities rules in federal and state public buildings, with civil suits and possible trespass arrest; detention, if it occurs, carries documented abuse. National hate-crime and employment protections and court injunctions are partial and do not reach the visitor-facing facilities or border practices. A family with a trans minor also faces the state care ban and school restroom rule. The worst documented feature is tier-1 universal facilities exclusion, compounded by tier-2 custody harm, placing the jurisdiction in the high-risk range rather than the criminalization extreme.
